title.narrative: Cotton as a common: joint regenerative cotton sourcing strategy in workwear and hygiene solutions

description.narrative: The Social Sustainability Fund - SF project, led by the consortium comprising Raddis Stichting, GVK Society, Yasasree Viroha Impex Pvt Ltd, and Dutch companies HAVEP workwear and Yassasree B.V., aims to establish socially just and environmentally responsible cotton value chains in India. The project has a focus on eradicating social issues, particularly child labour, absence of living wage & living income and unsafe working conditions in cotton supply chains, where India has specific high risk in these area. The consortium plans to address these issues by joining hands in a joint sourcing of regenerative cotton in India. The partners, with proven success in related projects, demonstrate a holistic understanding of the complex socio-economic drivers in the cotton sector. The project's novelty lies in addressing backend processes and social risks in TIER 3 (ginning, spinning, logistics) and TIER 4 (seed production, farming, logistics). Instead of building on an existing opaque supply chain that relies on certain tools such as certification and third party audits, the consortium opt for a redesigned supply chain starting with transparent regenerative cotton cultivation to use as the basis for the local impact assessment. This forms the basis for real opportunities for improvement through implementation in Phase B. The development of a joint action plan is anticipated, aligning departments, involving local stakeholders, and leveraging existing networks. Due diligence research will examine corporate connections and gaps. Communication strategies include engagement within partner networks and broader industry events. The consortium embraces the goal of knowledge sharing in global supply chains, aligning with the Social Sustainability Fund's mission.
